facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a benign reading is the issuer's own net leverage of 2.53x and the 3.10x ratio of debt plus lease liabilities to reported EBITDA, both above the 2.27x headline; the strongest evidence for it is interest cover of 4.58x and nine-month levered free cash flow of USD 1,063 million. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- No instrument list is printed at 30 September 2026: the nine-month 2026 report gives debt totals, movements and maturity bands only, so the instrument register stops at 31 December 2025, the movements table records only the 2026 borrowings and repayments that the report describes, and the debt stack cannot be drawn; this is High severity because it blocks structural priority and refinancing work, and the action is to obtain the third-quarter 2026 debt schedule. - No source states a legal rank, security or guarantor ladder for any facility beyond the titles senior notes and the senior unsecured wording for the Swedish krona bond, the redeemed Paraguay notes and one term loan, and the indentures and credit agreements are listed as exhibits but not supplied; the debt stack is therefore a single not-supplied row, this is High severity for ranking and covenant work, and the action is to supply the executed documents. - Undrawn committed facilities at 30 September 2026 are not established: no 2026 report mentions the USD 600 million revolving facility, and searches for revolving, undrawn, committed, standby and letters of credit found only the 2025 statement and a separate USD 65 million facility of the Chile associate; liquidity at that date is cash only, this is High severity, and the action is a treasury or lender confirmation. - Contractual principal at 30 September 2026 is not stated: the maturity bands add to USD 8,647 million against a printed total of USD 8,648 million and the filing prints no issuance costs, so the reconciling item is rounding only; at year-end 2025 principal exceeded carrying value by USD 51 million, so principal is probably above the carrying figures shown; this is Medium severity and the action is to obtain the principal schedule. - Last-twelve-month EBITDA is not pro forma for Coltel before 6 February 2026 and the issuer prints no pro forma EBITDA, so the ratios at 30 September 2026 overstate leverage on that one point, while the exclusion of lease costs understates it; the fiscal-year figure also includes the Paraguay mobile finance business that the nine-month 2025 column excludes; this is Medium severity and the action is to obtain the issuer's pro forma bridge. - Closing Cash is not supplied for FY2025, 9M 2025 or 9M 2026 because the cash flow statement prints a separate effect of disposed or held-for-sale cash of 8, 8 and 6 that the fixed rows cannot hold, so opening cash plus the net change does not reach the printed balance; the balance-sheet cash is stated, this is Low severity, and no action is needed beyond reading the printed statement. - Total Liabilities is not supplied for FY2025 or 9M 2026 because the printed total liabilities plus total equity exceed printed total assets by one million in both columns; this is the filing's own rounding, it is Low severity, and the action is to read the printed total liabilities of 13,633 and 18,432 with that limitation. - Lines the filing prints as a dash are carried as not supplied rather than zero: Sale of Lati Operations for 9M 2026, profit from discontinued operations for FY2025 and acquisitions of subsidiaries for 9M 2025; this is Low severity and the action is to read the dash as nil only after confirming with the issuer. - No statement of financial position at 30 September 2025 is in the supplied filings, so debt, net debt and the ratios at that date are not calculated; the issuer's own series shows 6,260 of gross debt and 2.09x leverage at that date; this is Medium severity and the action is to supply the third-quarter 2025 report. - Gross profit, cost of sales and selling and administrative expense are not printed because the income statement is by nature; this is Low severity and no action is needed. - The leverage ratios in the financial metrics table are not calculated for the nine-month columns because nine-month EBITDA is not an annual figure, and the date and cash total of the October 2026 dividend instalment are not stated, so that row of the post-balance-sheet table gives only the figures the balance sheet supports; this is Low severity and the action is to obtain the instalment amounts. - Several cells of the KPI dashboard are not stated: the fixed-rate share of debt at four quarter ends, the one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA for four quarters and Coltel's quarterly Adjusted EBITDA are not in the nine-month 2026 report; this is Low severity and the action is to read the earlier quarterly releases if a series is needed. - Principal, drawn amount, commitment, security, ranking, annual amortisation and for most loans the rate, reference rate and spread are not stated per instrument in the 2025 annual report; each is marked not supplied in the instrument register; this is Medium severity and the action is to supply the debt agreements. - Covenant levels and any 2026 compliance statement are not supplied: the annual report states that no covenant breach occurred at 31 December 2025 and none is expected in the next twelve months, but the 2026 reports are silent; this is High severity for covenant work and the action is to supply the covenant definitions and certificates. - The terms of the USD 2,101 million of payables and accruals for capital expenditure, including interest, due dates and whether any is supplier finance, are not stated; this is Medium severity because it is a large claim outside debt, and the action is to obtain the schedule. - Coltel purchase accounting remains provisional and the Ecuador measurement period ended on 30 October 2026 with the accounting not yet finalised at the report date, so goodwill, lease liabilities and property values may be restated; this is Low severity and the action is to read the fourth-quarter 2026 report. - The quarterly interim reports for the first and second quarters of 2026 were used only to cross-check the gross debt, net debt and leverage series, which they confirm; the revolving facility maturity differs between the annual report note and its exhibit list as recorded in the conflict register; this is Low severity.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Control rests with one family group, and creditors should read every capital decision with that in mind. Atlas Investissement, ultimately owned by the Niel family, held 42.2% of the voting shares excluding treasury shares at 31 December 2025, and the Niel family group reported 44.1% including shares it expected to buy by 30 June 2026. Four of eight directors are affiliated with it, the company is not a controlled company under Nasdaq rules because the holding is below 50%, and the annual report itself says the holder can influence director elections and corporate actions. The consequence for creditors is that dividend, acquisition and related-party decisions can reflect the shareholder's priorities, while the board's audit committee, which is wholly independent, is the main check. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Shareholder distributions are large against current earnings and absorb most free cash flow. Declared dividends were USD 1,048 million in 2025, against net profit attributable to owners of USD 1,316 million, and USD 755 million in nine months 2026, against net profit attributable to owners of USD 316 million and equity free cash flow of USD 867 million, so declared dividends were 0.87x equity free cash flow. A dividend payable of USD 579 million sat on the balance sheet at 30 September 2026 and the board states a policy of sustaining or growing dividends while maintaining a prudent capital structure. The mechanism is that payouts competing with acquisition funding and debt repayment for the same cash leave little retained cash to reduce leverage, and dividends are limited to distributable reserves, with USD 757 million of retained profits at 30 September 2026 not distributable. facts.text: Acquisitions have changed the perimeter faster than the disclosure can follow. The group bought Uruguay and Ecuador in October 2025 for enterprise values of USD 440 million and USD 380 million, completed the buy-out of its Colombian partner for about USD 571 million on 29 January 2026, closed the purchase of Coltel on 6 February 2026 for about USD 214.4 million, and bought the remaining Coltel shares on 27 April 2026. Reported nine-month revenue rose 55.2% while organic growth was 4.4%, Coltel's and Ecuador's purchase accounting is provisional, and management excluded Uruguay and Ecuador from its 2025 internal control assessment. The consequence is integration and restructuring cost, with Colombia carrying USD 116 million of one-off costs in nine months, and growth figures that cannot be read like for like. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings are concentrated in two countries. Guatemala supplied 20.32% of consolidated segment revenue and 24.34% of consolidated segment Adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026, and Colombia, now two segments, supplied 38.37% and 31.67%, so the two together are 58.69% of revenue and 56.01% of Adjusted EBITDA. The annual report states that the group's cash flow is highly dependent on Guatemala. The consequence is that a regulatory, currency or competitive shock in either country would reach the cash that services debt and funds dividends. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Related-party exposure to the controlling shareholder's group is small in flows but has two features worth monitoring. The balance sheet showed USD 195 million payable to the Iliad Holding group at 31 December 2025 against USD 2 million a year earlier, and the filings do not state what it is. Separately, the Chile acquisition in February 2026 was made through a vehicle owned 49% by Millicom and 51% by NJJ Cactus, which the filings do not describe as a related party although its name matches the NJJ Holding that the related-party note says Xavier Niel owns, with a Millicom call option in the fifth and sixth years and a later option for the partner to buy Millicom's interest. The consequence is that any later funding of those options or of the vehicle's losses, which already exceed Millicom's recognised interest by USD 41 million, would draw group cash, and whether that is a related-party use of cash is not established. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for lower risk is that all eight directors are non-executive, the audit committee consists only of independent directors and reviews related-party transactions, the auditor reported effective internal control, no amendment, priming or exchange affecting creditors is documented, and management has set a year-end 2026 leverage target of below 2.5x. The view would move to Low if the target is met while dividends stay within equity free cash flow, if the debt documents show restricted-payment limits that bind the shareholder, and if the Chile options are priced and funded without recourse to the group. It would move to High if declared dividends continue to exceed internally generated cash, if distributions or related-party funding are paid from new borrowing, or if the controlling shareholder's holding passes 50% and the group elects controlled-company exemptions. facts.text: Between October 2025 and April 2026 the group completed six acquisitions or buy-outs that together changed its scale, and it sold most of its tower portfolio. Uruguay (enterprise value USD 440 million, closed 7 October 2025) and Ecuador (enterprise value USD 380 million, closed 30 October 2025) added mobile operators and their debt and leases. In Colombia the group bought out its partner's UNE shares for about USD 571 million on 29 January 2026, acquired Telefonica's 67.5% of Coltel for about USD 214.4 million on 6 February 2026, of which USD 169 million had been paid at that date, and bought the remaining Coltel shares on 27 April 2026. Coltel brought USD 1,424 million of other debt and financing and USD 515 million of lease liabilities. facts.label: T2D.9 Sponsor risk assessment
facts.text: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by concentrated control and distributions that are large against free cash flow, because payouts and acquisitions compete with debt reduction for the same cash, which implies slower deleveraging and some exposure to shareholder priorities. Countervailing evidence is an independent audit committee, effective internal control, regular disclosure and no documented creditor-adverse action. Governance and sponsor assessment completed with limitations; key gaps are the debt documents, the Iliad Holding payable and the controlling shareholder's later holdings. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is adequate to strong because margins are high and the base is spread over eleven markets, but nearly all recent growth was bought. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 45.9% for nine months 2026, down from 47.3%, and postpaid customers were 30.79% of mobile customers against 21.10% a year earlier, which makes revenue more recurring. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is moderate on the statements but has risen faster than the headline suggests. Net debt before derivatives was USD 7,800 million, or 2.05x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, at 30 September 2026, against 1.83x at the end of 2025. Pro forma net debt would be USD 8,379 million, or 2.20x, once the dividend payable of USD 579 million is settled in cash from the October 2026 instalment onwards, and the 15 October 2026 Coltel loan swap leaves it at USD 7,800 million, or 2.05x; pro forma cash after the dividend settlement is not established. The issuer's own net leverage, which adds derivatives and vendor financing, deducts lease costs and is pro forma for acquisitions, was 2.53x against 2.17x at the end of 2025. A lease liability of USD 3,190 million and capital expenditure payables of USD 2,101 million sit outside debt, so creditors face more fixed claims than the ratio shows. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C07; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32

facts.text: Liquidity is the weakest dimension. Cash of USD 848 million was 0.97x the USD 872 million of debt due within one year, against 4.72x at the end of 2025, with USD 986 million due in the following year, and the USD 600 million revolving facility matures in October 2027 with its availability after 2025 not established. Funding access is nonetheless real: during 2026 the group raised development-bank and bond funding, reopened its 2032 senior notes and added bank loans in several countries, and the annual report records a Moody's rating of Ba2 with a stable outlook and a Fitch rating of BB+ at year-end 2025. The consequence is that refinancing depends on market and bank access staying open for about USD 1,858 million over two years, with no committed cushion shown for the period after 2025. facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: Millicom sells mobile and fixed services under the Tigo brand in eleven Latin American markets, and mobile generated 60% of 2025 service revenue with fixed and other services at 38%. Postpaid and fixed subscriptions give recurring monthly revenue, whereas prepaid customers buy packages that expire after days to weeks, so the postpaid share, 30.79% of mobile customers, matters for cash-flow visibility. Most towers were sold and leased back, which cut capital intensity but converted it into 15-year lease obligations, so lease payments were USD 483 million in nine months 2026, and Coltel added a large share of the mobile customer base in 2026. The consequence is a business with recurring revenue and heavy fixed charges, where debt service capacity depends on keeping the postpaid base and the margin. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is predictable in postpaid, fixed and business-to-business lines and cyclical in prepaid and equipment sales. Organic service revenue grew 5.3% in nine months 2026, helped by a more-for-more pricing strategy that raised mobile ARPU 19.0% in dollars, including currency effects, to USD 7.4 per month excluding Coltel, and postpaid customers excluding acquisitions grew. Fixed revenue is weaker underneath: excluding acquisitions the fixed revenue generating units would have declined because fixed telephony is shrinking, and home ARPU rose to USD 27.7 per month while the base would be shrinking without acquisitions. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Direct costs grew faster than revenue in the third quarter, up 72.4% against revenue growth of 60.8%, on acquisitions, bad debt and World Cup programming, while operating expenses rose 57.4% including USD 20 million of Colombian restructuring. Severance of about USD 111 million was recorded in Colombia, and one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA were USD 149 million for nine months. Lease, interest and spectrum charges sit below Adjusted EBITDA and do not flex with volume, so the cash margin after them is more sensitive than the EBITDA margin: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 47.3% to 45.9%, or 1.4 percentage points, in nine months even with 5.3% organic service revenue growth. Margins can be defended against volume pressure only if integration savings arrive; the filings state no savings target, so resilience is not established beyond the Guatemala margin of 56.09%, which includes a one-time reversal of legal provisions in the third quarter. Lease, interest and spectrum charges sit below Adjusted EBITDA and do not flex with volume, so the cash margin after them is more sensitive than the EBITDA margin: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 47.3% to 45.9%, or 1.4 percentage points, in nine months even with 5.3% organic service revenue growth. Margins can be defended against volume pressure only if integration savings arrive; the filings state no savings target, so resilience is not established beyond the Guatemala margin of 56.09%, which includes a one-time reversal of legal provisions in the third quarter.

Equity free cash flow converted 29.31% of Adjusted EBITDA, down from 32.48%, because lease payments, finance charges and USD 306 million of taxes rose with the perimeter. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense: the annual report names América Móvil, Telefónica and Liberty Latin America as main competitors with greater resources, adds WOM in Colombia, where competitors may hold a dominant position, and describes telecom services as largely commoditized, so competition on price can compress margin and raise churn. Entry is limited by the need for spectrum licences with fixed terms, which is an analyst inference, and several licences expire from 2026. Substitution is a risk mainly for pay-TV through wireless and satellite alternatives and for fixed telephony. Buyers have little to hold them in prepaid, where no contract is signed, but credit exposure to certain business customers, mainly governments, is concentrated. Suppliers matter through spectrum fees, the tower leaseback and programming content such as the World Cup. The consequence is that pricing power is clearest in Guatemala, where ARPU rose and margin is highest, and weakest in Colombia, the largest market. facts.label: Macro, currency and regulation
facts.text: These factors are material, so they are included. The strongest is currency: the Colombian peso, guarani and boliviano rose against the dollar over the year, which flattered reported revenue and profit while also raising the dollar value of local-currency debt, while the annual report warns that a significant amount of costs, capital expenditure and borrowings is in dollars. Bolivia moved from a fixed peg to a market regime and foreign exchange volatility remains elevated there. Higher energy prices from the Middle East conflict add inflation and cost pressure. On regulation, spectrum licences must be renewed against fees, the Costa Rican regulator blocked the planned merger and a USD 32 million goodwill impairment followed, and tax claims against subsidiaries are estimated at USD 378 million with provisions of USD 60 million. The consequence is that currency and regulation can move earnings and leverage in dollars without any change in operating performance. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: For the next twelve to twenty-four months, management guides to equity free cash flow of around USD 1.1 billion for 2026, which implies about USD 233 million in the fourth quarter after USD 867 million in nine months, and to year-end leverage below 2.5x. On the issuer's own figures, leverage of 2.53x needs net debt about USD 95 million lower, and the fourth-quarter cash left, if the October dividend matches the USD 126 million paid in the third quarter, is about USD 107 million, so headroom against the target is thin at roughly USD 12 million before currency effects and payments for acquisitions. Tailwinds are integration savings, higher postpaid mix and local-currency strength; headwinds are the World Cup content boost to home revenue, which is unlikely to recur, USD 1.50 per share of additional dividends in January and April 2027, spectrum payments, the maturity of the revolving facility in October 2027 and Chile losses. Over three to five years, maturities are USD 1,947 million in the third year, USD 1,601 million in the fourth and USD 1,147 million in the fifth, with USD 2,094 million after five years, and a management plan pays about USD 50 million only when equity free cash flow reaches USD 2 billion a year. The path to a stronger profile is therefore deleveraging through free cash flow growth, which depends on the board holding the dividend. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most plausible downside is a price war and asymmetric regulation in Colombia during integration, coinciding with a reversal of local currencies. The operating break comes first in Colombian ARPU and postpaid growth, where a competitor with a dominant position could cut prices. Revenue then grows below the 5.3% organic rate and Adjusted EBITDA margin falls because network and integration costs do not flex, while lease payments and finance charges of USD 915 million in nine months remain fixed claims on the cash that is left. Free cash flow falls below the dividend, and as an illustration each 10% fall in last-twelve-month reported EBITDA lifts net debt over EBITDA from 2.05x to 2.27x and a 20% fall lifts it to 2.56x. Liquidity is then tested by USD 872 million of maturities against cash of USD 848 million, a revolving facility that matures in October 2027 and USD 986 million due the year after. Management can cut or defer dividends that are not yet declared, defer capital expenditure, sell the mobile financial services business and draw development-bank funding, and market access in 2026 shows these routes are open. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within twelve months if refinancing stays available, but not if the revolving facility is drawn, because the cushion would then be gone. The observable triggers are Colombian service revenue growth, the margin, free cash flow against dividends and the refinancing of the next two years of maturities. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Millicom presents an adequate business profile supported by high margins, scale in eleven markets and a rising postpaid base, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-driven leverage, dividends that absorb 0.87x of equity free cash flow and earnings concentrated in Guatemala and Colombia. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because equity free cash flow is growing and guidance was raised, but it is thin after fixed charges and distributions. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on bank and development-bank access, on confirmation that the revolving facility is available and on the board holding the dividend while leverage falls to the target. The primary downside path is a Colombian price war and currency reversal that cut earnings while leases, interest and dividends continue. Further analysis would require the debt documents, the revolving facility's status, instrument-level terms and pro forma earnings of the acquired businesses. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: concentration of earnings combined with distributions that leave little cash for deleveraging. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The four supplied filings support a source-based credit assessment of Millicom as of 5 November 2026, but not covenant, guarantee or recovery work, because no indenture or credit agreement was supplied. Creditors should treat leverage, liquidity and maturity findings as resting on filed statements, and covenant headroom and structural priority as not established.

The set holds the audited 2025 annual report and three 2026 interim reports, the latest dated 5 November 2026, all in US dollars on a consistent accounting basis. The perimeter widened after 2025 through the Colombian, Ecuadorian and Uruguayan acquisitions, so 2026 and 2025 periods are not like for like. Debt after 2025 appears as totals, movements and maturity bands rather than an instrument list, so the debt stack at 30 September 2026 cannot be rebuilt line by line, and the availability of the main revolving facility after 2025 is not stated.

spans.text: ## Request

MILLICOM INTERNATIONAL CELLULAR SA (issuer id tigo), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway (full credit assessment). The scope is Financial foundation: the income statement, cash flow, balance sheet, debt, net debt and credit-metric registers built from the four supplied filings, in US dollars millions.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025, with audited consolidated financial statements | 2026-03-24 | 13be2a8c900b103376e04c45e18282d28f2b1aac3516bfaed99fc02cc0e15f37 | Audited FY2025 statements, debt and financing note, instrument list at 2025-12-31, net debt, liquidity statement, covenant statement, FY2024 comparatives for revenue and Adjusted EBITDA |

| 6-K_2026-05-12_dp246578_6k.htm.jsonl | Form 6-K furnishing unaudited interim financial statements for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and the Q1 2026 earnings release | 2026-05-12 | e31fa18185d3ceef7ba9e0133efc952dd4f43ccbd999e9a5f5b5af04d8dbf712 | Cross-check of the quarterly gross debt, net debt and leverage series; Chile associate revolving facility; not used for a table figure |

| 6-K_2026-08-06_dp251442_6k.htm.jsonl | Form 6-K furnishing unaudited, independently reviewed interim financial statements for the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Q2 2026 earnings release and a press release | 2026-08-06 | 76b47ade3b6a5a2f060db2592b816c6ed584aa9ed405d036c0be893943dc1c51 | Cross-check of the quarterly net debt and leverage series and of the review conclusion; not used for a table figure |

| 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl | Form 6-K furnishing unaudited interim financial statements for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Q3 2026 earnings release and a press release | 2026-11-05 | 6ab7c7e5e635829f16eb15a89301463e6131db3f5c0e68ee118ba6350801f894 | Nine-month 2026 and 2025 statements, 2026-09-30 balance sheet, debt movements and maturity bands, issuer net debt and leverage, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, subsequent events, KPIs |
| Module | Document | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Accepted source-readiness module output for this run | feddc445c04747edb1b77c28793b2a836beb8190289c8edc129f0106940768a7 | Source gate, perimeter, restatement and gap findings carried forward; no figure copied without a source locator |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage looks moderate on the statements, with debt at 2.27x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, but the ratio understates creditor exposure because lease liabilities of USD 3,190 million sit outside debt and EBITDA is struck before lease costs. Debt rose from USD 6,886 million at 31 December 2025 to USD 8,648 million at 30 September 2026 while cash fell from USD 1,552 million to USD 848 million, so net debt before derivatives rose from USD 5,334 million to USD 7,800 million.

Basis: calculation K10; calculation K11; calculation K12; calculation K14; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 245; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 25

The issuer's own net leverage of 2.53x, which deducts lease costs from EBITDA, adds derivatives to net debt and is pro forma for acquisitions, is the better guide, and interest cover on reported EBITDA is 4.58x. Availability of the USD 600 million revolving facility after 2025 and any instrument-level debt detail are not established, so liquidity and ranking conclusions rest on year-end 2025 data.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation K13; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 255
### Leverage and coverage

Debt of USD 8,648 million is 2.27x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA of USD 3,813 million and 2.31x issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,743 million; at 31 December 2025 the same ratios were 2.36x and 2.50x. EBITDA grew faster than debt, mostly through acquisitions: the issuer reports nine-month Adjusted EBITDA growth of 50.6%, of which 8.8% is organic. The last twelve months include Ecuador and Uruguay from October 2025 and Coltel only from 6 February 2026, while the balance sheet carries the debt of all three in full, so on a pro forma basis the ratio would be lower, which partly offsets the lease effect. Adding lease liabilities of USD 3,190 million to debt gives 3.10x reported EBITDA, against 3.25x at year-end 2025.
Basis: calculation K04; calculation K05; calculation K12; calculation K14; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 3

Cash interest paid including lease interest was USD 832 million over the last twelve months, so reported EBITDA covers it 4.58x, down from 4.99x for 2025 because interest rose faster than EBITDA; on interest paid on debt alone cover is 6.82x. Cover is also more exposed to rates than a year ago: the issuer states that 56% of total debt is at fixed rates, against 70% at year-end 2025, mainly because Coltel's variable-rate debt was added.
Basis: calculation K07; calculation K08; calculation K13; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32
### Cash flow and claims outside debt

Operating cash flow was USD 2,028 million in nine months 2026 against cash capex of USD 965 million on spectrum, other intangibles and property, plant and equipment, leaving levered free cash flow of USD 1,063 million before USD 267 million of lease principal and USD 587 million of dividends. Acquisitions of subsidiaries took a further USD 924 million and, with dividends and lease principal, outweighed free cash flow, so cash fell by USD 698 million in the period.
Basis: calculation K17; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Two claims sit outside debt. Lease liabilities were USD 3,190 million at 30 September 2026, and payables and accruals for capital expenditure were USD 2,101 million against USD 1,198 million at year-end 2025, an increase of USD 903 million whose interest terms the filings do not state. A dividend payable of USD 579 million is a current liability, with declared instalments scheduled from October 2026 to April 2027, and it is not in net debt.
Basis: calculation K14; calculation K18; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Liquidity and maturities

Cash of USD 848 million does not cover the USD 872 million of debt due within one year, and a further USD 986 million falls due in the following year. The largest dated band is USD 1,947 million in the year to September 2029, and USD 2,094 million falls after September 2031. Undrawn committed facilities at 30 September 2026 are not established; at year-end 2025 cash plus the undrawn revolving facility was USD 2,152 million against USD 329 million due within one year.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation K19; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 255; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 272
### Definitions and data quality

The issuer's 2.53x is not comparable with 2.05x here. Its net debt adds USD 183 million of derivatives and vendor financing to debt, and its EBITDA is after lease depreciation and lease interest and pro forma for acquisitions, whereas the ratios in this module use balance-sheet debt less cash over reported EBITDA before lease costs. Operating cash flow is USD 2,028 million in the cash flow statement and USD 2,019 million in the issuer's free cash flow reconciliation, a difference of USD 9 million that the filing does not explain.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 40; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation K20

December 2025 comparatives were restated after the Uruguay and Ecuador purchase accounting was finalised, and the filings print one-million rounding differences between statement totals and their parts. The registers below use the audited 2025 figures for the 2025 column and record the restated figures where they differ.
### Subsequent events

On 15 October 2026 Coltel borrowed about USD 12.5 million from BTG Pactual and prepaid about USD 12.5 million to Banco Santander, which leaves net debt unchanged. The dividend payable of USD 579 million would raise net debt to USD 8,379 million, or 2.20x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, if settled from cash.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation K21
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a benign reading is the issuer's own net leverage of 2.53x and the 3.10x ratio of debt plus lease liabilities to reported EBITDA, both above the 2.27x headline; the strongest evidence for it is interest cover of 4.58x and nine-month levered free cash flow of USD 1,063 million. The view would improve if the issuer confirms that the USD 600 million revolving facility is still undrawn, if its pro forma EBITDA shows leverage at or below its year-end target of 2.5x, and if the dividend payable of USD 579 million is covered by free cash flow rather than cash. It would worsen if the revolving facility has been drawn or the capital expenditure payables carry interest.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K17; calculation K18; calculation K21

- The 2026 reports are unaudited, and only the six-month statements carry an auditor's review conclusion, which is not an audit; the 2025 figures are audited but were later restated for Uruguay and Ecuador purchase accounting.

- Reported EBITDA is calculated from operating profit and depreciation and amortization because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA, and it includes equity-accounted profit; the last-twelve-month figures are not pro forma and mix two treatments of the Paraguay mobile finance business.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 40; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation K04

- No instrument list, legal rank, security, guarantor scope, covenant level or 2026 compliance statement is supplied, and the availability of the USD 600 million revolving facility at 30 September 2026 is not stated, so liquidity, ranking and covenant conclusions are not established.

## Gaps

- No instrument list is printed at 30 September 2026: the nine-month 2026 report gives debt totals, movements and maturity bands only, so the instrument register stops at 31 December 2025, the movements table records only the 2026 borrowings and repayments that the report describes, and the debt stack cannot be drawn; this is High severity because it blocks structural priority and refinancing work, and the action is to obtain the third-quarter 2026 debt schedule.

- No source states a legal rank, security or guarantor ladder for any facility beyond the titles senior notes and the senior unsecured wording for the Swedish krona bond, the redeemed Paraguay notes and one term loan, and the indentures and credit agreements are listed as exhibits but not supplied; the debt stack is therefore a single not-supplied row, this is High severity for ranking and covenant work, and the action is to supply the executed documents.

- Undrawn committed facilities at 30 September 2026 are not established: no 2026 report mentions the USD 600 million revolving facility, and searches for revolving, undrawn, committed, standby and letters of credit found only the 2025 statement and a separate USD 65 million facility of the Chile associate; liquidity at that date is cash only, this is High severity, and the action is a treasury or lender confirmation.

- Contractual principal at 30 September 2026 is not stated: the maturity bands add to USD 8,647 million against a printed total of USD 8,648 million and the filing prints no issuance costs, so the reconciling item is rounding only; at year-end 2025 principal exceeded carrying value by USD 51 million, so principal is probably above the carrying figures shown; this is Medium severity and the action is to obtain the principal schedule.

- Last-twelve-month EBITDA is not pro forma for Coltel before 6 February 2026 and the issuer prints no pro forma EBITDA, so the ratios at 30 September 2026 overstate leverage on that one point, while the exclusion of lease costs understates it; the fiscal-year figure also includes the Paraguay mobile finance business that the nine-month 2025 column excludes; this is Medium severity and the action is to obtain the issuer's pro forma bridge.

- Closing Cash is not supplied for FY2025, 9M 2025 or 9M 2026 because the cash flow statement prints a separate effect of disposed or held-for-sale cash of 8, 8 and 6 that the fixed rows cannot hold, so opening cash plus the net change does not reach the printed balance; the balance-sheet cash is stated, this is Low severity, and no action is needed beyond reading the printed statement.

- Total Liabilities is not supplied for FY2025 or 9M 2026 because the printed total liabilities plus total equity exceed printed total assets by one million in both columns; this is the filing's own rounding, it is Low severity, and the action is to read the printed total liabilities of 13,633 and 18,432 with that limitation.

- Lines the filing prints as a dash are carried as not supplied rather than zero: Sale of Lati Operations for 9M 2026, profit from discontinued operations for FY2025 and acquisitions of subsidiaries for 9M 2025; this is Low severity and the action is to read the dash as nil only after confirming with the issuer.

- No statement of financial position at 30 September 2025 is in the supplied filings, so debt, net debt and the ratios at that date are not calculated; the issuer's own series shows 6,260 of gross debt and 2.09x leverage at that date; this is Medium severity and the action is to supply the third-quarter 2025 report.
- Gross profit, cost of sales and selling and administrative expense are not printed because the income statement is by nature; this is Low severity and no action is needed.

- The leverage ratios in the financial metrics table are not calculated for the nine-month columns because nine-month EBITDA is not an annual figure, and the date and cash total of the October 2026 dividend instalment are not stated, so that row of the post-balance-sheet table gives only the figures the balance sheet supports; this is Low severity and the action is to obtain the instalment amounts.

- Several cells of the KPI dashboard are not stated: the fixed-rate share of debt at four quarter ends, the one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA for four quarters and Coltel's quarterly Adjusted EBITDA are not in the nine-month 2026 report; this is Low severity and the action is to read the earlier quarterly releases if a series is needed.

- Principal, drawn amount, commitment, security, ranking, annual amortisation and for most loans the rate, reference rate and spread are not stated per instrument in the 2025 annual report; each is marked not supplied in the instrument register; this is Medium severity and the action is to supply the debt agreements.

- Covenant levels and any 2026 compliance statement are not supplied: the annual report states that no covenant breach occurred at 31 December 2025 and none is expected in the next twelve months, but the 2026 reports are silent; this is High severity for covenant work and the action is to supply the covenant definitions and certificates.

- The terms of the USD 2,101 million of payables and accruals for capital expenditure, including interest, due dates and whether any is supplier finance, are not stated; this is Medium severity because it is a large claim outside debt, and the action is to obtain the schedule.

- Coltel purchase accounting remains provisional and the Ecuador measurement period ended on 30 October 2026 with the accounting not yet finalised at the report date, so goodwill, lease liabilities and property values may be restated; this is Low severity and the action is to read the fourth-quarter 2026 report.

- The quarterly interim reports for the first and second quarters of 2026 were used only to cross-check the gross debt, net debt and leverage series, which they confirm; the revolving facility maturity differs between the annual report note and its exhibit list as recorded in the conflict register; this is Low severity.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance and business facts support a Medium sponsor and governance risk for creditors: the largest shareholder holds 42.2% of the voting shares and is affiliated with four of eight directors, and distributions are large while acquisitions have enlarged the group. Dividends declared were USD 1,048 million in 2025 and USD 755 million in the first nine months of 2026, which compares with equity free cash flow of USD 867 million for the same nine months.

Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 198; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation B05

The business is a diversified Latin American mobile and fixed operator with 60% of 2025 service revenue from mobile, but the annual report states that cash generation depends heavily on Guatemala, and the 2026 purchases in Colombia made Colombia the largest segment. Control, related-party balances and the absence of supplied debt documents leave creditor protections not established.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation B03; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Control rests with one family group, and creditors should read every capital decision with that in mind. Atlas Investissement, ultimately owned by the Niel family, held 42.2% of the voting shares excluding treasury shares at 31 December 2025, and the Niel family group reported 44.1% including shares it expected to buy by 30 June 2026. Four of eight directors are affiliated with it, the company is not a controlled company under Nasdaq rules because the holding is below 50%, and the annual report itself says the holder can influence director elections and corporate actions. The consequence for creditors is that dividend, acquisition and related-party decisions can reflect the shareholder's priorities, while the board's audit committee, which is wholly independent, is the main check.

Shareholder distributions are large against current earnings and absorb most free cash flow. Declared dividends were USD 1,048 million in 2025, against net profit attributable to owners of USD 1,316 million, and USD 755 million in nine months 2026, against net profit attributable to owners of USD 316 million and equity free cash flow of USD 867 million, so declared dividends were 0.87x equity free cash flow. A dividend payable of USD 579 million sat on the balance sheet at 30 September 2026 and the board states a policy of sustaining or growing dividends while maintaining a prudent capital structure. The mechanism is that payouts competing with acquisition funding and debt repayment for the same cash leave little retained cash to reduce leverage, and dividends are limited to distributable reserves, with USD 757 million of retained profits at 30 September 2026 not distributable.

Acquisitions have changed the perimeter faster than the disclosure can follow. The group bought Uruguay and Ecuador in October 2025 for enterprise values of USD 440 million and USD 380 million, completed the buy-out of its Colombian partner for about USD 571 million on 29 January 2026, closed the purchase of Coltel on 6 February 2026 for about USD 214.4 million, and bought the remaining Coltel shares on 27 April 2026. Reported nine-month revenue rose 55.2% while organic growth was 4.4%, Coltel's and Ecuador's purchase accounting is provisional, and management excluded Uruguay and Ecuador from its 2025 internal control assessment. The consequence is integration and restructuring cost, with Colombia carrying USD 116 million of one-off costs in nine months, and growth figures that cannot be read like for like.

Earnings are concentrated in two countries. Guatemala supplied 20.32% of consolidated segment revenue and 24.34% of consolidated segment Adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026, and Colombia, now two segments, supplied 38.37% and 31.67%, so the two together are 58.69% of revenue and 56.01% of Adjusted EBITDA. The annual report states that the group's cash flow is highly dependent on Guatemala. The consequence is that a regulatory, currency or competitive shock in either country would reach the cash that services debt and funds dividends.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation B03; calculation B04; calculation B06

Related-party exposure to the controlling shareholder's group is small in flows but has two features worth monitoring. The balance sheet showed USD 195 million payable to the Iliad Holding group at 31 December 2025 against USD 2 million a year earlier, and the filings do not state what it is. Separately, the Chile acquisition in February 2026 was made through a vehicle owned 49% by Millicom and 51% by NJJ Cactus, which the filings do not describe as a related party although its name matches the NJJ Holding that the related-party note says Xavier Niel owns, with a Millicom call option in the fifth and sixth years and a later option for the partner to buy Millicom's interest. The consequence is that any later funding of those options or of the vehicle's losses, which already exceed Millicom's recognised interest by USD 41 million, would draw group cash, and whether that is a related-party use of cash is not established.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for lower risk is that all eight directors are non-executive, the audit committee consists only of independent directors and reviews related-party transactions, the auditor reported effective internal control, no amendment, priming or exchange affecting creditors is documented, and management has set a year-end 2026 leverage target of below 2.5x. The view would move to Low if the target is met while dividends stay within equity free cash flow, if the debt documents show restricted-payment limits that bind the shareholder, and if the Chile options are priced and funded without recourse to the group. It would move to High if declared dividends continue to exceed internally generated cash, if distributions or related-party funding are paid from new borrowing, or if the controlling shareholder's holding passes 50% and the group elects controlled-company exemptions.
### Limitations

- No indenture, credit agreement or covenant definition was supplied, so the sponsor and governance level rests on observed behaviour and not on legal capacity to distribute, invest or release guarantees, and any statement about dividend capacity or priming risk is not established.

- The latest holding figures come from a March 2026 filing and the year-end 2025 report, so a change in the controlling shareholder's stake after those dates, which would alter the control assessment, is not established.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 157

- Purchase accounting for Coltel and Ecuador is provisional and pro forma figures are limited to incremental revenue and net profit, with no pro forma Adjusted EBITDA or leverage, so conclusions about how far acquisitions raised or lowered credit quality are directional only.

- The filings do not state what the USD 195 million payable to the Iliad Holding group is, so whether it is an unpaid dividend or another funding relationship, which would change the related-party reading, is not established.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 296

On the disposal side, the Lati tower sale to SBA and Atis Group brought total consideration of about USD 975 million and a gain of USD 741 million but created about USD 680 million of new lease assets and liabilities, and the sale of the Paraguay mobile finance business was agreed in January 2026 for a base price of USD 10 million.

New debt in 2026 included a COP 370,000 million eight-year private bond subscribed by the Inter-American Development Bank and Proparco on 27 March, an USD 87.5 million reopening of the 2032 senior notes on 14 April, and a series of variable-rate loans at Coltel and Tigo Colombia, while Tigo Paraguay redeemed its 2027 senior unsecured notes for about USD 139.7 million on 29 April. ## Gaps

- No indenture, credit agreement or covenant definition was supplied, so sponsor and governance conclusions rest on observed behaviour and the legal capacity to distribute, invest, prime or release guarantees is not established; this is High severity and the action is to supply the executed documents and covenant certificates.

- The filings do not state what the USD 195 million payable to the Iliad Holding group is or how it will be settled, so the related-party reading is incomplete; this is Medium severity and the action is to obtain the related-party note detail.

- Ownership is known to 31 December 2025 and, for the Niel family group, to a March 2026 filing, so the control assessment after that date is not established; this is Medium severity and the action is to check the latest ownership filing.

- The funding mix of the 2026 acquisitions and pro forma Adjusted EBITDA and leverage for Coltel, Ecuador and Uruguay are not printed (only incremental revenue and net profit are given), so the leverage effect of acquisitions is directional only; this is Medium severity and the action is to request the issuer's pro forma bridge.

- The annual report caps the Chile earn-outs at USD 150 million and the nine-month report at USD 490 million, and the option prices are set by formula, so the contingent cash is not sized, and the filings do not state whether NJJ Cactus is related to the controlling shareholder; this is Medium severity and the action is to confirm the contractual terms.

- The interest terms and schedule of most of the USD 2,101 million of capital expenditure payables at 30 September 2026 are not stated, because the annual report describes only USD 662 million of Colombian spectrum and licence payables at 31 December 2025, so a possible funding source outside debt cannot be fully assessed; this is Medium severity and the action is to obtain the payables schedule.

- No fee schedule, sponsor equity commitment or fund information exists for the controlling shareholder beyond USD 6 million of purchases, and sponsor fund vintage does not apply to a family holding, so extraction and exit-pressure inferences are not made; this is Low severity and no action is needed beyond a related-party fee schedule if wanted.

- The nine-month report gives different customer, homes-passed and employee totals in its earnings release and press release footer, and describes the Honduras repatriation of USD 79 million as both a three-month and a nine-month figure; this is Low severity and the earnings release tables were used.

- The 2026 reports give no statement of covenant compliance, so covenant monitoring after 31 December 2025 is not established; this is High severity and the action is to supply compliance certificates.

spans.text: ## Request

MILLICOM INTERNATIONAL CELLULAR SA (issuer id tigo), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway (full credit assessment). The scope is Fundamental credit: the integrated view of business quality, cash generation, liquidity, refinancing capacity and financial policy, built from the four supplied filings and the three earlier modules.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025, with audited consolidated financial statements | 2026-03-24 | 13be2a8c900b103376e04c45e18282d28f2b1aac3516bfaed99fc02cc0e15f37 | Competition, currency, regulation and spectrum risk factors, revenue model, ratings statement, liquidity facility, non-recourse debt, Colombian spectrum payables |

| 6-K_2026-08-06_dp251442_6k.htm.jsonl | Form 6-K furnishing unaudited, independently reviewed interim financial statements for the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Q2 2026 earnings release and a press release | 2026-08-06 | 76b47ade3b6a5a2f060db2592b816c6ed584aa9ed405d036c0be893943dc1c51 | Raised 2026 equity free cash flow guidance and lowered year-end leverage target |

| Financial foundation (CP-1) | Accepted financial-foundation module output for this run | 6e20ddd95bc1308c2bc09ebca0cc251a694b26f0523e71cc2390cf77e3992778 | Net debt, leverage, interest cover, maturity bands, claims outside debt and post-balance-sheet adjustments |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Millicom presents an adequate credit profile, with strong margins and a larger operating base, but creditors carry leverage that rose with acquisitions, dividends that absorb most free cash flow and earnings concentrated in two countries.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C05; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Adjusted EBITDA margin was 45.9% for nine months 2026 and equity free cash flow was USD 867 million, yet declared dividends were 0.87x of that cash flow and the issuer's own net leverage was 2.53x against a year-end target below 2.5x. Liquidity rests on a revolving facility whose availability after 2025 is not established, and no debt documents were supplied, so protections for creditors are not established.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 31; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C14
### Key findings

The business is adequate to strong because margins are high and the base is spread over eleven markets, but nearly all recent growth was bought. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 45.9% for nine months 2026, down from 47.3%, and postpaid customers were 30.79% of mobile customers against 21.10% a year earlier, which makes revenue more recurring. Reported revenue rose 55.2% while organic growth was 4.4%, so the larger scale mostly reflects Coltel, Ecuador and Uruguay and favourable currency moves rather than a stronger market position. The consequence for creditors is that earnings quality has to be judged on the organic rate and on how much of the acquired EBITDA turns into cash.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 28; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 33; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C01; calculation C02

Leverage is moderate on the statements but has risen faster than the headline suggests. Net debt before derivatives was USD 7,800 million, or 2.05x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, at 30 September 2026, against 1.83x at the end of 2025. Pro forma net debt would be USD 8,379 million, or 2.20x, once the dividend payable of USD 579 million is settled in cash from the October 2026 instalment onwards, and the 15 October 2026 Coltel loan swap leaves it at USD 7,800 million, or 2.05x; pro forma cash after the dividend settlement is not established. The issuer's own net leverage, which adds derivatives and vendor financing, deducts lease costs and is pro forma for acquisitions, was 2.53x against 2.17x at the end of 2025. A lease liability of USD 3,190 million and capital expenditure payables of USD 2,101 million sit outside debt, so creditors face more fixed claims than the ratio shows.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C07; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32

Cash generation is solid but largely distributed, so deleveraging depends on the dividend as much as on operations. Equity free cash flow was USD 867 million, up 36.0% from USD 638 million, yet it equals only 29.31% of Adjusted EBITDA against 32.48% a year earlier, mainly because lease payments of USD 483 million and finance charges of USD 432 million together took 30.93% of Adjusted EBITDA against 28.26%. Declared dividends of USD 755 million were 0.87x equity free cash flow and left only USD 112 million, so cash cannot reduce debt materially while the payout continues.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 31; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C03; calculation C04

Liquidity is the weakest dimension. Cash of USD 848 million was 0.97x the USD 872 million of debt due within one year, against 4.72x at the end of 2025, with USD 986 million due in the following year, and the USD 600 million revolving facility matures in October 2027 with its availability after 2025 not established. Funding access is nonetheless real: during 2026 the group raised development-bank and bond funding, reopened its 2032 senior notes and added bank loans in several countries, and the annual report records a Moody's rating of Ba2 with a stable outlook and a Fitch rating of BB+ at year-end 2025. The consequence is that refinancing depends on market and bank access staying open for about USD 1,858 million over two years, with no committed cushion shown for the period after 2025.

Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 255; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 273; calculation C08

Earnings are concentrated, and currency moves flatter reported growth. Guatemala and Colombia together supplied 58.69% of segment revenue and 56.01% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, and the annual report states that group cash flow is highly dependent on Guatemala. The Colombian peso, Paraguayan guarani and Bolivian boliviano rose 25.4%, 22.7% and 17.1% against the US dollar over the year, which lifted reported results, while costs, capital expenditure and 38.99% of debt are in US dollars. A reversal would cut earnings in dollars, partly offset by a smaller dollar value of local-currency debt, but would leave dollar debt and dollar costs unchanged.

Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 33; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C09; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Financial policy is the main judgemental drag, consistent with a Medium sponsor and governance risk. One family group holds 42.2% of the voting shares and four of eight directors are affiliated with it, shareholders approved dividends of USD 3.00 per share payable to April 2027 and the board added an interim USD 1.50 per share, and the senior management plan communicated in October 2026 rewards equity free cash flow of USD 2 billion with no leverage condition stated. Policy therefore leaves the outcome for creditors to the board's discretion rather than to a documented restriction.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 20; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 28

Colombia is the swing factor for the next two years. It is now the largest segment at 38.37% of segment revenue but earned a nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin of 38.65% against 56.09% in Guatemala, after one-off costs of USD 116 million in nine months, and it faces competitors with substantially greater resources, including América Móvil, and a regulator that may impose asymmetric rules on a larger market share. If integration savings arrive the margin gap narrows and cash conversion improves; if competition forces price cuts the gap persists on the largest revenue base.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 41; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C06; calculation C10
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that the issuer's net leverage fell from 2.73x at June 2026 to 2.53x at September 2026, that 2026 equity free cash flow guidance was raised to around USD 1.1 billion and the year-end target lowered to below 2.5x, that interest is covered 4.58x by reported EBITDA, that 61.01% of debt is in local currencies that match revenue, and that dividends are discretionary rather than contractual and fell from 1.65x of equity free cash flow in nine months 2025 to 0.87x. The view would improve to a strong profile if year-end leverage comes in below 2.5x with dividends covered by equity free cash flow and the revolving facility is confirmed undrawn. It would weaken if equity free cash flow falls below declared dividends, if year-end leverage stays above 2.5x, if a Colombian price war or a currency reversal cuts Adjusted EBITDA, or if refinancing of the USD 1,858 million due within two years is delayed or priced above the issuer's average interest rate of 8.3%.

Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 29; 6-K_2026-08-06_dp251442_6k.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C03; calculation C08; calculation C11; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Limitations

- The weakest-dimension finding on liquidity would change if the revolving facility is undrawn and available, because cash plus that facility would then cover the next year's maturities; the filings do not state its status after 2025.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 255; calculation C08

- The financial policy conclusion rests on observed distributions and acquisitions; without the debt documents, whether such payments are permitted, limited or restricted is not established, and that would move the view on governance either way.
Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 258; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The year-end target headroom uses a net leverage denominator that the issuer does not print and that is derived here from its ratio and net debt, so the estimate carries rounding error and is directional only.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C11

- Growth quality is read from the issuer's organic rates, which remove currency and the Colombian consolidation; no pro forma Adjusted EBITDA is printed for the acquisitions, so how much acquired earnings is durable is not established.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is margin. Adjusted EBITDA margin of 45.9% for nine months 2026 means each dollar of revenue leaves a large cushion for lease, interest and tax charges, which is why interest cover stays at 4.58x despite higher debt; the margin is down from 47.3% a year earlier on acquisitions, so the cushion is thinner than before.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C01; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second strength is a more recurring revenue base. Postpaid customers rose to 30.79% of mobile customers, and prepaid customers, who buy short packages and sign no contract, are being migrated, which supports revenue visibility and lowers churn exposure in Guatemala, Panama and Paraguay.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 33; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 35; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C02

The third strength is funding access matched to local revenue. 61.01% of gross debt is in local currencies, and 2026 saw a development-bank bond, a reopening of the 2032 senior notes and local bank loans, so the group can raise money across currencies, which reduces the risk that one market closes refinancing.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C09

The fourth strength is rising cash generation. Equity free cash flow rose 36.0% to USD 867 million, guidance for 2026 was raised to around USD 1.1 billion, and issuer net leverage fell from 2.73x to 2.53x in the third quarter, which shows that operations can reduce leverage when dividends are covered.
The first weakness is concentration. Guatemala and Colombia supply 56.01% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, so a shock in either market reaches the cash that services debt and funds dividends.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 17; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C10

The second weakness is liquidity against maturities. Cash of USD 848 million is 0.97x the debt due in a year, so the group relies on refinancing and on a revolving facility whose availability is not established.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C08
The third weakness is distributions: declared dividends were 0.87x equity free cash flow, which slows deleveraging and lets a controlling shareholder's priorities shape credit outcomes.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 20; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 31; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03

The fourth weakness is fixed claims outside debt. Lease liabilities of USD 3,190 million and capital expenditure payables of USD 2,101 million raise charges that do not flex, and lease payments plus finance charges took 30.93% of Adjusted EBITDA against 28.26%.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C04; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The fifth weakness is the quality of growth. Reported revenue rose 55.2% against 4.4% organically, integration cost USD 149 million of one-off items in nine months and acquired businesses have provisional accounting, so a faster slowdown than organic trends would be a surprise only to those reading reported growth.

### Company description and credit linkage

Millicom sells mobile and fixed services under the Tigo brand in eleven Latin American markets, and mobile generated 60% of 2025 service revenue with fixed and other services at 38%. Postpaid and fixed subscriptions give recurring monthly revenue, whereas prepaid customers buy packages that expire after days to weeks, so the postpaid share, 30.79% of mobile customers, matters for cash-flow visibility. Most towers were sold and leased back, which cut capital intensity but converted it into 15-year lease obligations, so lease payments were USD 483 million in nine months 2026, and Coltel added a large share of the mobile customer base in 2026. The consequence is a business with recurring revenue and heavy fixed charges, where debt service capacity depends on keeping the postpaid base and the margin.

Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 79–80; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 31; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C02; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

Atlas Investissement, ultimately owned by the Niel family, holds 42.2% of the voting shares and four of eight directors are affiliated with it, so one holder can influence director elections and corporate actions without owning a majority. The Luxembourg parent depends on subsidiaries to send it cash, and about 70% of gross debt sits at the operating entities with the other 30% at corporate level, so parent creditors rank behind operating-company lenders except where the parent guarantees that debt, and guarantees and legal rank are not established. The Honduras joint venture, in which Millicom holds 66.67%, carries its own debt without recourse to the parent. The consequence is that cash reaching parent creditors depends on dividends and repatriation from subsidiaries, with USD 79 million repatriated from joint ventures and associates in nine months 2026, and on board decisions influenced by the largest shareholder.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C12
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is predictable in postpaid, fixed and business-to-business lines and cyclical in prepaid and equipment sales. Organic service revenue grew 5.3% in nine months 2026, helped by a more-for-more pricing strategy that raised mobile ARPU 19.0% in dollars, including currency effects, to USD 7.4 per month excluding Coltel, and postpaid customers excluding acquisitions grew. Fixed revenue is weaker underneath: excluding acquisitions the fixed revenue generating units would have declined because fixed telephony is shrinking, and home ARPU rose to USD 27.7 per month while the base would be shrinking without acquisitions. Competition on price and customer experience in markets with penetration above 100% limits further volume growth, so pricing power is moderate and the revenue outlook rests on mix migration rather than subscriber growth.
Basis: 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 28; 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl, page 33; 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation C02
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Direct costs grew faster than revenue in the third quarter, up 72.4% against revenue growth of 60.8%, on acquisitions, bad debt and World Cup programming, while operating expenses rose 57.4% including USD 20 million of Colombian restructuring. Severance of about USD 111 million was recorded in Colombia, and one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA were USD 149 million for nine months. Lease, interest and spectrum charges sit below Adjusted EBITDA and do not flex with volume, so the cash margin after them is more sensitive than the EBITDA margin: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 47.3% to 45.9%, or 1.4 percentage points, in nine months even with 5.3% organic service revenue growth. Margins can be defended against volume pressure only if integration savings arrive; the filings state no savings target, so resilience is not established beyond the Guatemala margin of 56.09%, which includes a one-time reversal of legal provisions in the third quarter.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital expenditure excluding spectrum was USD 757 million and spectrum paid USD 207 million in nine months 2026, together 14.97% of revenue, and fixed commitments to buy network equipment and intangibles were USD 384 million, of which USD 367 million fall due within a year against USD 305 million at the end of 2025. Equity free cash flow converted 29.31% of Adjusted EBITDA, down from 32.48%, because lease payments, finance charges and USD 306 million of taxes rose with the perimeter. Colombian spectrum payables of USD 662 million at the end of 2025 fall due in instalments to 2037. Capex can be deferred in the near term, but spectrum and lease charges cannot, so the cash that supports debt service is what remains after fixed charges, and it is already largely paid out in dividends.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense: the annual report names América Móvil, Telefónica and Liberty Latin America as main competitors with greater resources, adds WOM in Colombia, where competitors may hold a dominant position, and describes telecom services as largely commoditized, so competition on price can compress margin and raise churn. Entry is limited by the need for spectrum licences with fixed terms, which is an analyst inference, and several licences expire from 2026. Substitution is a risk mainly for pay-TV through wireless and satellite alternatives and for fixed telephony. Buyers have little to hold them in prepaid, where no contract is signed, but credit exposure to certain business customers, mainly governments, is concentrated. Suppliers matter through spectrum fees, the tower leaseback and programming content such as the World Cup. The consequence is that pricing power is clearest in Guatemala, where ARPU rose and margin is highest, and weakest in Colombia, the largest market.
### Macro, currency and regulation

These factors are material, so they are included. The strongest is currency: the Colombian peso, guarani and boliviano rose against the dollar over the year, which flattered reported revenue and profit while also raising the dollar value of local-currency debt, while the annual report warns that a significant amount of costs, capital expenditure and borrowings is in dollars. Bolivia moved from a fixed peg to a market regime and foreign exchange volatility remains elevated there. Higher energy prices from the Middle East conflict add inflation and cost pressure. On regulation, spectrum licences must be renewed against fees, the Costa Rican regulator blocked the planned merger and a USD 32 million goodwill impairment followed, and tax claims against subsidiaries are estimated at USD 378 million with provisions of USD 60 million. The consequence is that currency and regulation can move earnings and leverage in dollars without any change in operating performance.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are the 45.9% margin, scale across eleven markets, a rising postpaid share and funding in several currencies. Weaknesses are concentration in Guatemala and Colombia, cash of USD 848 million against USD 872 million of debt due in a year, distributions that absorb 0.87x of free cash flow and claims outside debt. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are integration savings in Colombia, a partial sale of the mobile financial services business and a leverage target below 2.5x. Threats that could weaken it are a Colombian price war, currency reversal, regulatory asymmetry and a further large acquisition or related-party commitment.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next twelve to twenty-four months, management guides to equity free cash flow of around USD 1.1 billion for 2026, which implies about USD 233 million in the fourth quarter after USD 867 million in nine months, and to year-end leverage below 2.5x. On the issuer's own figures, leverage of 2.53x needs net debt about USD 95 million lower, and the fourth-quarter cash left, if the October dividend matches the USD 126 million paid in the third quarter, is about USD 107 million, so headroom against the target is thin at roughly USD 12 million before currency effects and payments for acquisitions. Tailwinds are integration savings, higher postpaid mix and local-currency strength; headwinds are the World Cup content boost to home revenue, which is unlikely to recur, USD 1.50 per share of additional dividends in January and April 2027, spectrum payments, the maturity of the revolving facility in October 2027 and Chile losses. Over three to five years, maturities are USD 1,947 million in the third year, USD 1,601 million in the fourth and USD 1,147 million in the fifth, with USD 2,094 million after five years, and a management plan pays about USD 50 million only when equity free cash flow reaches USD 2 billion a year. The path to a stronger profile is therefore deleveraging through free cash flow growth, which depends on the board holding the dividend.

### Downside scenario

The most plausible downside is a price war and asymmetric regulation in Colombia during integration, coinciding with a reversal of local currencies. The operating break comes first in Colombian ARPU and postpaid growth, where a competitor with a dominant position could cut prices. Revenue then grows below the 5.3% organic rate and Adjusted EBITDA margin falls because network and integration costs do not flex, while lease payments and finance charges of USD 915 million in nine months remain fixed claims on the cash that is left. Free cash flow falls below the dividend, and as an illustration each 10% fall in last-twelve-month reported EBITDA lifts net debt over EBITDA from 2.05x to 2.27x and a 20% fall lifts it to 2.56x. Liquidity is then tested by USD 872 million of maturities against cash of USD 848 million, a revolving facility that matures in October 2027 and USD 986 million due the year after. Management can cut or defer dividends that are not yet declared, defer capital expenditure, sell the mobile financial services business and draw development-bank funding, and market access in 2026 shows these routes are open. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within twelve months if refinancing stays available, but not if the revolving facility is drawn, because the cushion would then be gone. The observable triggers are Colombian service revenue growth, the margin, free cash flow against dividends and the refinancing of the next two years of maturities.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Millicom presents an adequate business profile supported by high margins, scale in eleven markets and a rising postpaid base, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-driven leverage, dividends that absorb 0.87x of equity free cash flow and earnings concentrated in Guatemala and Colombia. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because equity free cash flow is growing and guidance was raised, but it is thin after fixed charges and distributions. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on bank and development-bank access, on confirmation that the revolving facility is available and on the board holding the dividend while leverage falls to the target. The primary downside path is a Colombian price war and currency reversal that cut earnings while leases, interest and dividends continue. Further analysis would require the debt documents, the revolving facility's status, instrument-level terms and pro forma earnings of the acquired businesses. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: concentration of earnings combined with distributions that leave little cash for deleveraging.
